CHANHASSEN, Minn., Sept. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- From protein-maxxing on social media to an expanding array of high-protein foods on grocery shelves, protein is seemingly everywhere. So are conflicting claims about how much people need and when they should eat it. According to Anika Christ, a Registered Dietitian and Certified Personal Trainer at Life Time, there's a simple place to start: Aim for at least 30 grams of high-quality protein at every meal.

"Everyone wants to know the secret to building muscle, but it's not a secret," said Christ. "Strength training creates the opportunity. Protein helps your body do something with it. That's why we recommend starting with 30 grams of quality protein at every meal. It's simple, achievable and one of the most effective nutrition habits people can build."

This guideline is one of the daily habits at the heart of Life Time's upcoming 30 Strong Challenge, a complimentary coaching plan for Life Time club members that runs from October 5th to November 3rd. The challenge draws on Life Time's more than three decades of experience helping people build healthy habits through nutrition education, coaching and fitness programming. The challenge returns for its third year after drawing over 66,000 participants in 2025 and is designed to help members rebuild consistency heading into the fall and winter seasons

Along with hitting 30 grams of protein per meal, participants work through other sustainable daily habits, including completing a workout, reaching 8,000 steps, drinking half their body weight in ounces of water, getting seven or more hours of sleep, taking time for self-care and spending time outside.
Incorporating 30 grams of protein in each meal can be achieved through a variety of animal- and plant-based sources, including:
A standard grilled chicken breast (30 grams)
Roasted turkey breast (34 grams – four ounces)
6-ounce steak (42 grams)
1.5 cups of extra-firm tofu (30 grams)
Five hard-boiled eggs (approximately 6 grams each)
One cup of cottage cheese (30 grams)

Whole foods for protein are a priority, but protein powders can also offer a convenient option for busy parents and professionals as a boost between meals.
